attacks.text: Put 2 damage counters on each of your opponent's Pokémon that has any damage counters on it.

cards.flavorText: It strikes at humans from total darkness. Those licked by its cold tongue grow weaker with each passing day until they die.
cards.name: Haunter

abilities.name: Gnawing Curse
abilities.text: Whenever your opponent attaches an Energy card from their hand to 1 of their Pokémon, put 2 damage counters on that Pokémon.

attacks.name: Fade to Black
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Should you feel yourself attacked by a sudden chill, it is evidence of an approaching Gengar. There is no escaping it. Give up.
cards.name: Gengar

attacks.name: Confuse Ray
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: It will use any means necessary to frighten people and absorb their life energy. It practices constantly to hone its skill in causing fear.
cards.name: Misdreavus

attacks.name: Chaos Wheel
attacks.text: Your opponent can't play any Pokémon Tool, Special Energy, or Stadium cards from their hand during their next turn.

attacks.name: Dark Arts
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each card in your opponent's hand.

cards.flavorText: It appears as if from nowhere—muttering incantations, placing curses, and giving people terrifying visions.
cards.name: Mismagius

cards.flavorText: It bounces constantly, using its tail like a spring. The shock of bouncing keeps its heart beating.
cards.name: Spoink

abilities.name: Own Tempo
abilities.text: This Pokémon can't be Confused.

attacks.name: Psych Up
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon's Psych Up attack does 60 more damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: It uses black pearls to amplify its psychic power. It does a strange dance to control foes' minds.
cards.name: Grumpig

attacks.name: Bell of Silence
attacks.text: Your opponent can't play any Pokémon that has an Ability from their hand during their next turn.

cards.flavorText: It uses the sucker on its head to hang from a tree or from eaves. It can produce seven different tones.
cards.name: Chimecho

attacks.name: Astonish
attacks.text: Choose a random card from your opponent's hand. Your opponent reveals that card and shuffles it into their deck.

cards.flavorText: The pumpkin body is inhabited by a spirit trapped in this world. As the sun sets, it becomes restless and active.
cards.name: Pumpkaboo

attacks.name: Confuse Ray
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Pumpkin Bomb
attacks.text: Before doing damage, you may discard any number of Pokémon Tool cards from your Pokémon. This attack does 40 more damage for each card you discarded in this way.

cards.flavorText: Singing in eerie voices, they wander town streets on the night of the new moon. Anyone who hears their song is cursed.
cards.name: Gourgeist

attacks.name: Singe
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

cards.flavorText: It burns its bodily fluids to create a poisonous gas. When its enemies become disoriented from inhaling the gas, it attacks them.
cards.name: Salandit

attacks.name: Nasty Plot
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 cards and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Severe Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned. Put 4 damage counters instead of 1 on that Pokémon between turns.

cards.flavorText: For some reason, only females have been found. It creates a reverse harem of male Salandit that it lives with.
cards.name: Salazzle

attacks.name: Fixer of the Forest
attacks.text: Put 3 Pokémon Tool cards from your discard pile into your hand.

cards.flavorText: Known for its extreme intelligence, this Pokémon will look down on inexperienced Trainers, so it's best suited to veteran Trainers.
cards.name: Oranguru

abilities.name: Empty Light
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may leave both Active Pokémon Confused and Poisoned.

attacks.name: Lock Up
attacks.text: The Defending Pokémon can't retreat during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Symbiont-GX
attacks.text: Add the top 2 cards of your opponent's deck to their Prize cards. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

cards.name: Nihilego-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Three-Step Strike
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: It can spontaneously become enraged. Everyone near it clears out as it rampages and the resulting loneliness makes it angrier still.
cards.name: Mankey

attacks.name: Lucha Fight
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon's attacks do 30 more damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: It has been known to become so angry that it dies as a result. Its face looks peaceful in death, however.
cards.name: Primeape

attacks.name: Leer
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: When it thinks of its deceased mother, it weeps loudly. Mandibuzz that hear its cries will attack it from the air.
cards.name: Cubone

abilities.name: Rock Peak Growl
abilities.text: Your Registeel's attacks do 10 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Tough Swing
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Resistance.

cards.flavorText: Its entire body is made of rock. If any part chips off in battle, it attaches rocks to repair itself.
cards.name: Regirock

attacks.name: Eerie Fluid
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Earthquake
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage to each of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: It has strong regenerative capabilities. Even if parts of it are bitten off by fish Pokémon, it will return to normal within a few hours.
cards.name: Gastrodon

cards.flavorText: Despite its adorable appearance, when it gets angry and flails about, its arms and legs could knock a pro wrestler sprawling.
cards.name: Stufful

abilities.name: Fluffy
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from the attacks of your opponent's non-Fire Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Cross-Cut
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is an Evolution Pokémon, this attack does 60 more damage.

cards.flavorText: This immensely dangerous Pokémon possesses overwhelming physical strength. Its habitat is generally off-limits.
cards.name: Bewear

attacks.name: Jet Punch
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Knuckle Impact
attacks.text: This Pokémon can't attack during your next turn.

attacks.name: Absorption-GX
attacks.text: This attack does 40 damage for each of your remaining Prize cards. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

cards.name: Buzzwole-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

cards.flavorText: Around dawn, its ominous howl echoes through the area to announce that this is its territory.
cards.name: Houndour

attacks.name: Fire Fang
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

attacks.name: Puncturing Fangs
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Resistance.

cards.flavorText: Long ago, people imagined its eerie howls to be the call of the grim reaper.
cards.name: Houndoom

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: They cannot see, so they tackle and bite to learn about their surroundings. Their bodies are covered in wounds.
cards.name: Deino

attacks.name: Double Hit
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 60 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: The two heads do not get along. Whichever head eats more than the other gets to be the leader.
cards.name: Zweilous

abilities.name: Weed Out
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may choose 3 of your Benched Pokémon. Then, discard your other Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Dark Destruction
attacks.text: You may discard an Energy from this Pokémon. If you do, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The heads on their arms do not have brains. They use all three heads to consume and destroy everything.
cards.name: Hydreigon

attacks.name: Eat Sloppily
attacks.text: Discard the top 5 cards of your deck. If any of those cards are Energy cards, attach them to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Glutton-GX

attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Crunch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.
cards.name: Mawile

cards.flavorText: It usually lives deep in mountains. However, hunger may drive it to eat railroad tracks and cars.
cards.name: Aron

cards.flavorText: It loves iron ore. Groups of them fight for territory by bashing one another with their steel bodies.
cards.name: Lairon

attacks.name: Revenge Cannon
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each damage counter on all of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Buster Swing
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Resistance.

cards.flavorText: It claims an entire mountain as its own. The more wounds it has, the more it has battled, so don't take it lightly.
cards.name: Aggron

attacks.name: Turbo Arm
attacks.text: Attach a basic Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Iron Hand
attacks.text: If Regice is on your Bench, heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Tempered by pressure underground over tens of thousands of years, its body cannot be scratched.
cards.name: Registeel

attacks.name: Fury Attack
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

attacks.name: Iron Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: Wearing the shell covering they stole from Shelmet, they defend themselves and attack with two lances.
cards.name: Escavalier

abilities.name: Slice Off
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may discard a Special Energy from 1 of your opponent's Pokémon.

attacks.name: Gale Blade
attacks.text: You may shuffle this Pokémon and all cards attached to it into your deck.

attacks.name: Blade-GX
attacks.text: Take a Prize card. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

cards.name: Kartana-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Double Slap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: It hugely inflates its stomach and sings a mysterious melody. If you hear this melody, you'll become sleepy right away.
cards.name: Jigglypuff

attacks.name: Hypnoblast
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Punishing Slap
attacks.text: If any of your opponent's Pokémon have any Darkness Energy attached to them, this attack does 60 more damage.

cards.flavorText: It sheds its fine fur when the seasons change. The fur is gathered and spun into a luxurious yarn.
cards.name: Wigglytuff

attacks.name: Lead
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Supporter card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Bright Horns
attacks.text: This Pokémon can't use Bright Horns during your next turn.

cards.flavorText: Legends say it can share eternal life. It slept for a thousand years in the form of a tree before its revival.
cards.name: Xerneas

attacks.name: Tropical Head
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage times the amount of Energy attached to this Pokémon to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Dragon Hammer
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Tower-Go-Round-GX
attacks.text: Move any number of Energy from your Pokémon to your other Pokémon in any way you like. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

cards.name: Alolan Exeggutor-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

cards.flavorText: It expresses its feelings by smacking its scales. Metallic sounds echo through the tall mountains where Jangmo-o lives.
cards.name: Jangmo-o

attacks.name: Noble Roar
attacks.text: Your opponent switches their Active Pokémon with 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: It leaps at its prey with a courageous shout. Its scaly punches tear its opponents to shreds.
cards.name: Hakamo-o

attacks.name: War Cry
attacks.text: If you have fewer Pokémon in play than your opponent, this attack does 90 more damage.

attacks.name: Clanging Scales
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 more damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: When it spots enemies, it threatens them by jingling the scales on its tail. Weak opponents will crack and flee in panic.
cards.name: Kommo-o

abilities.name: Moomoo Malt
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is your Active Pokémon, whenever you attach an Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Pokémon, heal 90 damage from that Pokémon.

attacks.name: Sitdown Splash
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Its milk is high in calories and packed with nutrients. Therefore, if you drink too much of it, you may wind up with a body like Miltank's.
cards.name: Miltank

cards.flavorText: For some reason, it likes to land on people's heads softly and act like it's a hat.
cards.name: Swablu

attacks.name: Draco Melody
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, search your deck for a Dragon Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Cotton Guard
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: It flies gracefully through the sky. Its melodic humming makes you feel like you're in a dream.
cards.name: Altaria

attacks.name: Bug Search
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand.

cards.flavorText: They flock in great numbers. Though small, they flap their wings with great power.
cards.name: Starly

cards.flavorText: They maintain huge flocks, although fierce scuffles break out between various flocks.
cards.name: Staravia

attacks.name: Clutch
attacks.text: The Defending Pokémon can't retreat during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Sky Hunting
attacks.text: If your opponent's Pokémon is Knocked Out by the damage from this attack, switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The muscles in its wings and legs are strong. It can easily fly while gripping a small Pokémon.
cards.name: Staraptor

abilities.name: Seal of Antiquity
abilities.text: This Pokémon can't attack unless Regirock, Regice, and Registeel are on your Bench.

attacks.name: Giant Stomp
attacks.text: Discard any Stadium card in play.

cards.flavorText: It is said to have made Pokémon that look like itself from a special ice mountain, rocks, and magma.
cards.name: Regigigas

cards.name: Regigigas

attacks.name: Tickle
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: Minccino greet each other by grooming one another thoroughly with their tails.
cards.name: Minccino

attacks.name: Amazing Plea
attacks.text: Choose 2 cards from your discard pile. Then, ask your opponent if you may put them into your hand. If yes, put those cards into your hand. If no, this attack does 80 damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Their white fur feels amazing to touch. Their fur repels dust and prevents static electricity from building up.
cards.name: Cinccino

cards.flavorText: They use their large ears to dig burrows. They will dig the whole night through.
cards.name: Bunnelby

attacks.name: Dig
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to this Pokémon during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Hammer Arm
attacks.text: Discard the top card of your opponent's deck.

cards.flavorText: With their powerful ears, they can heft boulders of a ton or more with ease. They can be a big help at construction sites.
cards.name: Diggersby

attacks.name: Armor Press
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: The heavy control mask it wears suppresses its intrinsic capabilities. This Pokémon has some hidden special power.

attacks.name: Mad Party
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each Pokémon in your discard pile that has the Mad Party attack.

cards.name: Polteageist

cards.flavorText: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.
cards.name: Hatterene

attacks.name: Aromatherapy

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.

attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: These intelligent Pokémon touch horns with each other to share information between them.

cards.flavorText: It's capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.
cards.name: Drakloak

attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

attacks.text: This Pokémon can't use Meteor Assault again until it leaves the Active Spot.

cards.flavorText: Only Farfetch'd that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon's leek withers, it will retire from combat.

cards.flavorText: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.

cards.flavorText: On the night of a full moon, if shadows move on their own and laugh, it must be Gengar's doing.
cards.name: Gengar

attacks.name: Tricky Slap
attacks.text: You and your opponent play Rock-Paper-Scissors until someone wins. If you win, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage from and effects of attacks done to this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The behavior of this clown-like Pokémon reminds one of pantomime. It creates invisible walls using a force emitted from its fingertips.
cards.name: Mr. Mime

attacks.name: Alluring Dance
attacks.text: Switch 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon with their Active Pokémon. The new Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Its strange cries sound like human language. There are some musicians who compose songs for Jynx to sing.
cards.name: Jynx

abilities.name: Loving Veil
abilities.text: All of your Pokémon take 20 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon V (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Psychic
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: It has the power to predict the future. Its power peaks when it is protecting its Trainer.
cards.name: Radiant Gardevoir
rules: Radiant Pokémon Rule: You can't have more than 1 Radiant Pokémon in your deck.

attacks.name: Lost Mine
attacks.text: You can use this attack only if you have 10 or more cards in the Lost Zone. Put 12 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is feared. When its gemstone eyes begin to glow with a sinister shine, it's believed that Sableye will steal people's spirits away.
cards.name: Sableye

attacks.name: Tempting Trap
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat. During your next turn, the Defending Pokémon takes 90 more damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.
cards.name: Mawile

cards.flavorText: There's a proverb that says, "Shun the house where Shuppet gather in the growing dusk."
cards.name: Shuppet

abilities.name: Puppet Offering
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may put a Supporter card from your discard pile into your hand. If you do, put this Pokémon in the Lost Zone. (Discard all attached cards.)

cards.flavorText: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.
cards.name: Banette

attacks.name: Moonglow Reverse
attacks.text: Move 2 damage counters from each of your Pokémon to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Those who sleep holding Cresselia's feather are assured of joyful dreams. It is said to represent the crescent moon.
cards.name: Cresselia

attacks.name: Collect
attacks.text: Draw a card.

cards.flavorText: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.
cards.name: Hisuian Zorua

attacks.name: Doom Curse
attacks.text: At the end of your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon will be Knocked Out.

attacks.name: Call Back
attacks.text: Put a card from your discard pile into your hand.

cards.flavorText: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark's own body.
cards.name: Hisuian Zoroark

attacks.name: Fickle Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: It spins while making its luminescent spots flash. These spots allow it to communicate with others by using different patterns of light.
cards.name: Inkay

attacks.name: Synchro Kinesis
attacks.text: Each player reveals their hand. If a card in your opponent's hand has the same name as a card in your hand, this attack does 90 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Gazing at its luminescent spots will quickly induce a hypnotic state, putting the observer under Malamar's control.
cards.name: Malamar

abilities.name: Flower Selecting
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, you may look at the top 2 cards of your deck and put 1 of them into your hand. Put the other card in the Lost Zone.

cards.flavorText: Comfey picks flowers with its vine and decorates itself with them. For some reason, flowers won't wither once they're attached to a Comfey.
cards.name: Comfey

attacks.name: Perplex
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Worst Gift
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage for each damage counter on all of your opponent's Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: It wears a rag fashioned into a Pikachu costume in an effort to look less scary. Unfortunately, the costume only makes it creepier.
cards.name: Mimikyu

attacks.name: Night Footsteps
attacks.text: Choose 2 of your opponent's Pokémon and put 2 damage counters on each of them.

attacks.name: Phantom Strike
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Phantom Strike.

cards.flavorText: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn't use its sense of sight. Spectrier's kicks are said to separate soul from body.
cards.name: Spectrier

abilities.name: Guardian of Love
abilities.text: Prevent all effects of your opponent's Pokémon's Abilities done to each of your Pokémon that has any Psychic Energy attached, except any Enamorus V.

attacks.name: Blossom Tail
attacks.text: Attach up to 2 basic Energy cards from your discard pile to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

cards.name: Enamorus V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Singe
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

cards.flavorText: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.
cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe

attacks.name: Very Vulnerable
attacks.text: If you have no cards in your hand, this attack does 150 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.
cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine

attacks.name: Split Spiral Punch
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Splash Loop
attacks.text: Put 2 Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand.

cards.flavorText: Its body is solid muscle. When swimming through cold seas, Poliwrath uses its impressive arms to smash through drift ice and plow forward.
cards.name: Poliwrath

cards.flavorText: Its whole body is composed of muscles. Even though it's the size of a human child, it can hurl 100 grown-ups.
cards.name: Machop

cards.flavorText: A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.
cards.name: Machoke

abilities.name: Crisis Muscles
abilities.text: If your opponent has 3 or fewer Prize cards remaining, this Pokémon gets +150 HP.

attacks.name: Strong-Arm Lariat
attacks.text: You may do 100 more damage. If you do, during your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

cards.flavorText: It quickly swings its four arms to rock its opponents with ceaseless punches and chops from all angles.
cards.name: Machamp

attacks.name: Take Down
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: Strong, but not too bright, this Pokémon can shatter even a skyscraper with its charging tackles.
cards.name: Rhyhorn

attacks.name: Take Down
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: It begins walking on its hind legs after evolution. It can punch holes through boulders with its horn.
cards.name: Rhydon

attacks.name: Geo Cannon
attacks.text: Discard the top card of your deck. If that card is an Energy card, this attack does 100 more damage, and attach that card to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Rocky Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: It can load up to three projectiles per arm into the holes in its hands. What launches out of those holes could be either rocks or Roggenrola.
cards.name: Rhyperior

attacks.name: Rock Crush
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Aerodactyl V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Lost Dive
attacks.text: Put the top 3 cards of your deck in the Lost Zone.

attacks.name: Ancient Star
attacks.text: Until this Pokémon leaves play, it gains an Ability that has the effect "Your opponent's Pokémon V in play, except any Aerodactyl VSTAR, have no Abilities." (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

cards.name: Aerodactyl VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Joust
attacks.text: Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Impound
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

cards.flavorText: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.
cards.name: Sudowoodo

attacks.name: Cyclone Pincers
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: It flies straight at its target's face, then clamps down on the startled victim to inject poison.
cards.name: Gligar

attacks.name: Hurricane Shock
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 50 damage for each heads. If at least 2 of them are heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: Its flight is soundless. It uses its lengthy tail to carry off its prey... Then its elongated fangs do the rest.
cards.name: Gliscor

attacks.name: Fake Out
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: There's a rumor of a traditional recipe for stew that Trainers can use to raise strong Makuhita.
cards.name: Makuhita

attacks.name: Shove
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Muscular Slap
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Resistance.

cards.flavorText: Hariyama that are big and fat aren't necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.
cards.name: Hariyama

attacks.name: Focus Fist
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: It eats just one berry a day. By enduring hunger, its spirit is tempered and made sharper.
cards.name: Meditite

attacks.name: Battle Step
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Fighting Energy cards and attach them to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: Through yoga training, it gained the psychic power to predict its foe's next move.
cards.name: Medicham

attacks.name: Into the Deep
attacks.text: Put up to 2 basic Energy cards from your discard pile into your hand.

cards.flavorText: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.
cards.name: Relicanth

attacks.name: Recover
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon and heal all damage from it.

attacks.name: Earthquake
attacks.text: This attack also does 20 damage to each of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: Its search for food sometimes leads it onto land, where it leaves behind a sticky trail of slime as it passes through.
cards.name: Gastrodon

cards.flavorText: In one minute, a well-trained Mienfoo can chop with its arms more than 100 times.
cards.name: Mienfoo

attacks.name: Double Smash
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 70 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: When Mienshao comes across a truly challenging opponent, it will lighten itself by biting off the fur on its arms.
cards.name: Mienshao

attacks.name: Smashing Edge
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.
cards.name: Landorus

cards.flavorText: After two Binacle find a suitably sized rock, they adhere themselves to it and live together. They cooperate to gather food during high tide.
cards.name: Binacle

abilities.name: Lost Block
abilities.text: Your opponent puts any Prize cards they would take in the Lost Zone instead of into their hand.

cards.flavorText: Seven Binacle come together to form one Barbaracle. The Binacle that serves as the head gives orders to those serving as the limbs.
cards.name: Barbaracle

attacks.name: Lucky Find
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Item cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: When beset by attackers, Carbink wipes them all out by firing high-energy beams from the gems embedded in its body.
cards.name: Carbink

attacks.name: Double Draw
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can bond very strongly with its Trainer, but it also has a habit of biting. Raising a Rockruff for a long time can be challenging.
cards.name: Rockruff

attacks.name: Fighting Headbutt
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness. If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Pokémon V, this attack does 50 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass's orders are absolute.
cards.name: Falinks

attacks.name: Power Stone
attacks.text: Attach up to 2 Fighting Energy cards from your hand to your Pokémon in any way you like.

attacks.name: Lost Shot
attacks.text: Put the top card of your opponent's deck in the Lost Zone.

cards.flavorText: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.
cards.name: Stonjourner

attacks.name: Poison Sting
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

cards.flavorText: Although the poison from its fangs isn't that strong, it's potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.
cards.name: Spinarak

attacks.name: String Bind
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

attacks.name: Venomous Fang
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

cards.flavorText: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.
cards.name: Ariados

cards.flavorText: It searches for shiny things for its boss. Murkrow's presence is said to be unlucky, so many people detest it.
cards.name: Murkrow

attacks.name: Night Cyclone
attacks.text: Move all Energy from this Pokémon to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

cards.flavorText: Its goons take care of most of the fighting for it. The only time it dirties its own hands is in delivering a final blow to finish off an opponent.
cards.name: Honchkrow

attacks.name: Sucker Punch and Turn
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Darkness Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Constant polishing makes the edge of the blade on its tail extremely sharp. It's Zangoose's archrival.
cards.name: Seviper

abilities.name: Cursed Message
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, search your deck for a card and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Chain of Spirits
attacks.text: This attack does 60 more damage for each Spiritomb in your discard pile.

cards.flavorText: Exactly 108 spirits gathered to become this Pokémon. Apparently there are some ill-natured spirits in the mix.
cards.name: Spiritomb

abilities.name: Wild Style
abilities.text: This Pokémon's attacks cost Colorless less for each of your opponent's Single Strike, Rapid Strike, and Fusion Strike Pokémon in play.

attacks.name: Dynamic Tail
attacks.text: This attack also does 60 damage to 1 of your Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.name: Drapion V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Hazard Star
abilities.text: During your turn, you may make your opponent's Active Pokémon Paralyzed and Poisoned. During Pokémon Checkup, put 3 damage counters on that Pokémon instead of 1. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Big Bang Arm
attacks.text: This attack does 10 less damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

cards.name: Drapion VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Nightmare
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Pitch-Black Blade
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

cards.flavorText: On a moonless night, a strange incident occurred in which every one of a village's inhabitants suffered nightmares. The villagers attested that Darkrai appeared before them in these nightmares.
cards.name: Darkrai

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: It spins while making its luminescent spots flash. These spots allow it to communicate with others by using different patterns of light.
cards.name: Inkay

attacks.name: Hand of Djinn
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Darkness Energy card and attach it to 1 of your Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: It gathers things it likes and passes them through its loop to teleport them to a secret place.
cards.name: Hoopa

abilities.name: Poison Peak
abilities.text: During Pokémon Checkup, put 2 more damage counters on your opponent's Poisoned Pokémon.

attacks.name: Poison Jab
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

cards.flavorText: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.
cards.name: Radiant Hisuian Sneasler
rules: Radiant Pokémon Rule: You can't have more than 1 Radiant Pokémon in your deck.

attacks.name: Energy Stream
attacks.text: Attach up to 2 Metal Energy cards from your discard pile to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Destructive Finish
attacks.text: Discard cards from the top of your deck until only 1 card remains. This attack does 30 more damage for each Energy card you discarded in this way.

cards.flavorText: It is said that if an Onix lives for over 100 years, its composition changes to become diamond-like.
cards.name: Radiant Steelix
rules: Radiant Pokémon Rule: You can't have more than 1 Radiant Pokémon in your deck.

cards.flavorText: It appears in ancient ruins. The pattern on its body doesn't come from any culture in the Galar region, so it remains shrouded in mystery.
cards.name: Bronzor

attacks.name: Gravitational Drop
attacks.text: This attack does 40 more damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

cards.flavorText: Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.
cards.name: Bronzong

attacks.name: Field Trap
attacks.text: If your opponent has a Stadium in play, discard it. If you discarded a Stadium in this way, discard 2 Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Living in mud with a high iron content has given it a strong steel body.
cards.name: Galarian Stunfisk

attacks.name: Windup Beam
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has a Pokémon Tool attached, this attack does 60 more damage, and your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Built roughly 500 years ago by a scientist, the part called the Soul-Heart is the actual life-form.
cards.name: Magearna

attacks.name: Feelin' Fine
attacks.text: Draw 3 cards.

attacks.name: Treasure Rush
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each card in your hand.

cards.name: Galarian Perrserker V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Abyss Seeking
attacks.text: Look at the top 4 cards of your deck and put 2 of them into your hand. Put the other cards in the Lost Zone.

attacks.name: Shred
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Giratina V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Lost Impact
attacks.text: Put 2 Energy attached to your Pokémon in the Lost Zone.

attacks.name: Star Requiem
attacks.text: You can use this attack only if you have 10 or more cards in the Lost Zone. Your opponent's Active Pokémon is Knocked Out. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

cards.name: Giratina VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

cards.flavorText: Goomy hides away in the shade of trees, where it's nice and humid. If the slime coating its body dries out, the Pokémon instantly becomes lethargic.
cards.name: Goomy

attacks.name: Rigidify
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 50 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui's water.
cards.name: Hisuian Sliggoo

abilities.name: Metal Lodging
abilities.text: Prevent all damage done to each of your Basic Pokémon that has any Metal Energy attached by attacks from your opponent's Pokémon V.

cards.flavorText: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.
cards.name: Hisuian Goodra

attacks.name: Slip-'n'-Trip
attacks.text: Your opponent switches their Active Pokémon with 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Rolling Shell
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Hisuian Goodra V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Moisture Star
abilities.text: During your turn, you may heal all damage from this Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Rolling Iron
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 80 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Hisuian Goodra VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Vanishing Wings
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if this Pokémon is on your Bench, you may shuffle it and all attached cards into your deck.

attacks.name: Flight Surf
attacks.text: If you have a Stadium in play, this attack does 80 more damage.

cards.name: Pidgeot V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

cards.flavorText: If this Pokémon's sticky saliva gets on you and you don't clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won't go away, either.
cards.name: Lickitung

cards.flavorText: Lickilicky's strange tongue can stretch to many times the length of its body. No one has figured out how Lickilicky's tongue can stretch so far.
cards.name: Lickilicky

attacks.name: Branch Calculation
attacks.text: Look at the top 4 cards of either player's deck and put them back in any order.

cards.flavorText: State-of-the-art technology was used to create Porygon. It was the first artificial Pokémon to be created via computer programming.
cards.name: Porygon

attacks.name: Garbage Attack
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each Pokémon Tool card in the Lost Zone (both yours and your opponent's).

cards.flavorText: This is a Porygon that was updated with special data. Porygon2 develops itself by learning about many different subjects all on its own.
cards.name: Porygon2

attacks.name: Downgrading Beam
attacks.text: Devolve 1 of your opponent's evolved Pokémon by removing any number of Evolution cards from it. Your opponent shuffles those cards into their deck.

cards.flavorText: Porygon-Z had a program installed to allow it to move between dimensions, but the program also caused instability in Porygon-Z's behavior.
cards.name: Porygon-Z

abilities.name: Unfazed Fat
abilities.text: Prevent all effects of attacks from your opponent's Pokémon done to this Pokémon. (Damage is not an effect.)

attacks.name: Thumping Snore
attacks.text: This Pokémon is now Asleep. During Pokémon Checkup, flip 2 coins instead of 1. If either of them is tails, this Pokémon is still Asleep.

cards.flavorText: It is not satisfied unless it eats over 880 pounds of food every day. When it is done eating, it goes promptly to sleep.
cards.name: Snorlax

attacks.name: Mischievous Tail
attacks.text: Look at the top card of your opponent's deck. You may have your opponent shuffle their deck.

cards.flavorText: This treetop dweller possesses a tail as dexterous as a hand. Ancient writings describe this Pokémon as a one-armed oddity.
cards.name: Aipom

attacks.name: All-You-Can-Grab
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. Search your deck for a number of cards up to the number of heads and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Knock Off
attacks.text: Discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

cards.flavorText: It uses its tails for everything. If it wraps both of its tails around you and gives you a squeeze, that's proof it really likes you.
cards.name: Ambipom

attacks.name: Void Return
attacks.text: You may switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Shadow Cyclone
attacks.text: Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.name: Hisuian Zoroark V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Phantom Star
abilities.text: During your turn, you may discard your hand and draw 7 cards. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Ticking Curse
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage for each of your Pokémon that has any damage counters on it.

cards.name: Hisuian Zoroark VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Lost Headbutt
attacks.text: Put an Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon in the Lost Zone.

cards.flavorText: These Pokémon can crush a car with no more than a headbutt. Bouffalant with more hair on their heads hold higher positions within the herd.
cards.name: Bouffalant

abilities.name: All Just a Dream
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is Asleep and is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, your opponent can't take any Prize cards for it.

attacks.name: Collapse
attacks.text: This Pokémon is now Asleep.

cards.flavorText: It remains asleep from birth to death as a result of the sedative properties of the leaves that form its diet.
cards.name: Komala

cards.flavorText: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.
cards.name: Skwovet

attacks.name: Collect
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

attacks.name: Spill Out
attacks.text: Discard your hand. If you discarded 5 or more cards in this way, this attack does 150 more damage.

cards.flavorText: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn't notice the loss.
cards.name: Greedent
Arc Phone
rules: Look at the top card of your deck. You may switch that card with 1 of your face-down Prize cards. (The cards stay face down.)
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

cards.name: Arezu
rules: Search your deck for up to 3 Evolution Pokémon that don't have a Rule Box, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. (Pokémon V, Pokémon-GX, etc. have Rule Boxes.)
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Box of Disaster
rules: If the Pokémon V this card is attached to has full HP and is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, put 8 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
Attach a Pokémon Tool to 1 of your Pokémon that doesn't already have a Pokémon Tool attached.

cards.name: Colress's Experiment
rules: Look at the top 5 cards of your deck and put 3 of them into your hand. Put the other cards in the Lost Zone.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.flavorText: After evolution, this Pokémon emerged onto land. Its lower body has become stronger, and blows from its tail are devastating.

attacks.name: Sandpot Trap

cards.flavorText: Palossand is known as the Beach Nightmare. It pulls its prey down into the sand by controlling the sand itself, and then it sucks out their souls.
cards.name: Palossand

cards.flavorText: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.
cards.name: Stonjourner

rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

cards.flavorText: It emits ultrasonic waves from its mouth to check its surroundings. Even in tight caves, Zubat flies around with skill.
cards.name: Zubat

cards.flavorText: It loves to drink other creatures' blood. It's said that if it finds others of its kind going hungry, it sometimes shares the blood it's gathered.
cards.name: Golbat

attacks.name: Diving Uppercut

cards.flavorText: It bounces toward opponents and gouges them with poisonous claws. No more than a scratch is needed to knock out its adversaries.
cards.name: Toxicroak

cards.name: Sandile

cards.name: Krokorok

abilities.name: Bully of the Sands

If this Pokémon is your Active Pokémon and is Knocked Out by damage from an opponent's attack, you may discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

attacks.name: Poison Sting

You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

cards.name: Hand Trimmer
rules: Each player discards cards from their hand until they have 5 cards in their hand. Your opponent discards first. (If a player has 5 or fewer cards in their hand, they do not discard.)
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

cards.name: Heavy Baton
rules: If the Pokémon this card is attached to has a Retreat Cost of exactly 4, is in the Active Spot, and is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, move up to 3 Basic Energy cards from that Pokémon to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

cards.name: Hero's Cape
rules: The Pokémon this card is attached to gets +100 HP.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

cards.name: Master Ball
rules: Search your deck for a Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

cards.name: Maximum Belt
rules: Attacks used by the Pokémon this card is attached to do 50 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon ex (before applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

cards.name: Morty's Conviction
rules: You can use this card only if you discard another card from your hand.  Draw a card for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Perilous Jungle
rules: During Pokémon Checkup, put 2 more damage counters on each Poisoned non-Darkness Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's).
You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it next to the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.
You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it into the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

cards.name: Prime Catcher
rules: Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot. If you do, switch your Active Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

cards.name: Reboot Pod
rules: Attach a Basic Energy card from your discard pile to each of your Future Pokémon.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

cards.name: Rescue Board
rules: The Retreat Cost of the Pokémon this card is attached to is Colorless less. If that Pokémon's remaining HP is 30 or less, it has no Retreat Cost.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

cards.name: Salvatore
rules: Search your deck for a card that has no Abilities and evolves from 1 of your Pokémon, and put it onto that Pokémon to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck. You can use this card on a Pokémon you put down when you were setting up to play or on a Pokémon that was put into play this turn.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Mist Energy
rules: As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides Colorless Energy.    Prevent all effects of attacks used by your opponent's Pokémon done to the Pokémon this card is attached to. (Existing effects are not removed. Damage is not an effect.)

cards.name: Neo Upper Energy
rules: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

attacks.name: Expelling Tornado
attacks.text: Choose 3 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. If you do, shuffle all of your opponent's Benched Pokémon that you didn't choose, and all cards attached to those Pokémon, into their deck.

attacks.name: Energy Loop
attacks.text: Put an Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand.

cards.flavorText: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.
cards.name: Shiftry

attacks.name: Ramming Shell
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 20 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: It lives along water in forests. In the daytime, it leaves the forest to sunbathe its treed shell.
cards.name: Grotle

attacks.name: Leaf Litter Tackle
attacks.text: Discard a Grass Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In this form, Deerling have a softly sweet scent that lingers in the nose.
cards.name: Deerling

abilities.name: Changing Seasons
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for a Stadium card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: Sawsbuck in their Autumn Form are known for having very short tempers. The males fight each other incessantly.
cards.name: Sawsbuck

attacks.name: Fake Out
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.
cards.name: Litten

attacks.name: Powder Snow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

cards.flavorText: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.
cards.name: Snom

cards.flavorText: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.
cards.name: Charjabug

attacks.name: Mirror Attack
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Psychic Pokémon, this attack does 30 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Ancient people believed that the pattern on Bronzor's back contained a mysterious power.
cards.name: Bronzor

attacks.name: Summoning Gate
attacks.text: Look at the top 8 cards of your deck. You may put any number of Pokémon you find there onto your Bench. Shuffle the other cards back into your deck.

attacks.name: Brain Shake
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: While it could use its psychic abilities in battle, this Pokémon prefers to swing its powerful arms around to beat opponents into submission.
cards.name: Reuniclus

attacks.name: Mini Drain
attacks.text: Heal 10 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur's pollen.
cards.name: Cutiefly

abilities.name: Memory Dive
abilities.text: Each of your evolved Pokémon can use any attack from its previous Evolutions. (You still need the necessary Energy to use each attack.)

cards.flavorText: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.
cards.name: Relicanth

attacks.name: Wild Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 50 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: It's not uncommon for tunnels that appear to have formed naturally to actually be a result of Excadrill's rampant digging.
cards.name: Excadrill

attacks.name: Mud Stock
attacks.text: Attach a Basic Fighting Energy card from your discard pile to each of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: High Horsepower
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 40 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.
cards.name: Mudsdale

attacks.name: Panic Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned, Confused, and Poisoned.

cards.flavorText: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.
cards.name: Arbok

attacks.name: Mysterious Beam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: It wraps its opponent in its gas-like body, slowly weakening its prey by poisoning it through the skin.
cards.name: Gastly

attacks.name: Meteor Mash
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon's Meteor Mash attack does 60 more damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Luster Blast
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.
cards.name: Metagross

cards.flavorText: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.
cards.name: Meltan

attacks.name: Tongue Pull
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. Put up to 2 Basic Pokémon you find there onto your opponent's Bench.

cards.flavorText: If this Pokémon's sticky saliva gets on you and you don't clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won't go away, either.
cards.name: Lickitung

attacks.name: A Cappella
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: It mimics the cries of other Pokémon to trick them into thinking it's one of them. This way they won't attack it.
cards.name: Chatot

attacks.name: Cleaning Up
attacks.text: Discard up to 2 Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.
cards.name: Minccino

attacks.name: Special Roll
attacks.text: This attack does 70 damage for each Special Energy card attached to this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.
cards.name: Cinccino

attacks.name: Raging Cannon
attacks.text: If all of your Benched Pokémon have at least 1 damage counter on them, this attack does 120 more damage.

cards.flavorText: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.
cards.name: Drampa

cards.flavorText: Hidden beneath a tangle of vines that grows nonstop even if the vines are torn off, this Pokémon's true appearance remains a mystery.
cards.name: Tangela

abilities.name: Thicket Body
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Loom Over
attacks.text: This attack does 10 less damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Tangrowth has two arms that it can extend as it pleases. Recent research has shown that these arms are, in fact, bundles of vines.
cards.name: Tangrowth

attacks.name: Slow Crunch
attacks.text: Discard all Energy from this Pokémon. At the end of your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon will be Knocked Out.

cards.flavorText: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.
cards.name: Pinsir

cards.flavorText: Some fishers weave its sturdy thread into nets to catch fish Pokémon.
cards.name: Spinarak

abilities.name: Big Net
abilities.text: Your opponent's Active Evolution Pokémon's Retreat Cost is Colorless more.

attacks.name: String Bind
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

cards.flavorText: It wanders in search of food after darkness falls, never nesting in a specific place.
cards.name: Ariados

attacks.name: Bullet Seed
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: It is very weak. Its only means of defense is to shake its leaves desperately at its attacker.
cards.name: Sunkern

attacks.name: Redirected Sunlight
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage for each Fire Energy attached to all of your opponent's Pokémon.

attacks.name: Mega Drain
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.
cards.name: Sunflora

attacks.name: Body Slam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: With its herculean powers, it can easily throw around an object that is 100 times its own weight.
cards.name: Heracross

attacks.name: Quick Sign
attacks.text: If you go first, you can use this attack during your first turn. Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Coordinated Strike
attacks.text: If Illumise is on your Bench, this attack does 60 more damage.

cards.flavorText: It flashes the light on its rear to communicate with other Volbeat. It loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.
cards.name: Volbeat

attacks.name: Slowing Perfume
attacks.text: You can use this attack only if you go second, and only during your first turn. Shuffle 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon and all attached cards into their deck.

cards.flavorText: It guides Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. There are scholars who research the meaning of these signs.
cards.name: Illumise

attacks.name: Leaflet Blessings
attacks.text: Attach a Basic Grass Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Benched Pokémon. If you do, heal all damage from that Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The younger they are, the more they smell like fresh grass. With age, their fragrance takes on the odor of fallen leaves.
cards.name: Leafeon

attacks.name: Leech Seed
attacks.text: Heal 20 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon came to be when the spirit of a deceased child possessed a tree stump. It now wanders the forest searching for friends.
cards.name: Phantump

attacks.name: Giga Drain
attacks.text: Heal from this Pokémon the same amount of damage you did to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Trevenant is very kind to Pokémon living in the forest. It doesn't even care if these Pokémon take up residence in the greenery on its head.
cards.name: Trevenant

cards.flavorText: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.
cards.name: Grookey

abilities.name: Boom Boom Groove

cards.flavorText: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.
cards.name: Thwackey

attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, attacks used by the Defending Pokémon cost Colorless more, and its Retreat Cost is Colorless more.

cards.flavorText: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.
cards.name: Rillaboom

attacks.name: Tumbling Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.
cards.name: Applin

attacks.name: Do the Wave
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.
cards.name: Dipplin

attacks.text: Put up to 2 Pokémon from your discard pile into your hand.

As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides Metal Energy.

The Metal Pokémon this card is attached to has no Retreat Cost.

As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides Fire Energy.
 
If this card is discarded by an effect of an attack used by the Fire Pokémon this card is attached to, put this card into your hand after attack damage and effects.
